You are given a Minimum Latency Problem (MLP).
The input describes a depot and a set of locations, each with coordinates. A single vehicle starts at the depot and must visit every location. The quality of a tour is measured by the sum of arrival times (latencies) at all locations.

You will receive the instance in the following format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Your task is to propose a single tour that starts at the depot, visits every location (and typically returns to the depot), aiming to minimize the sum of arrival times.

Return your decision in **exactly** this JSON format:
```json
{
  "solution": [depot_id, location_id, ..., depot_id]
}
```
Here, `solution` is the sequence of node identifiers in visiting order, starting at the depot and usually returning to it. Use **exactly** the same node identifiers that appear in the input. Do not include explanations or extra keys.

The van has to start at the hub and visit every address exactly once; no stops can be skipped or repeated. The specific addresses and timings are shown below.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of water meter locations that must be visited on the walking run (i.e., the number of nodes to cover). This counts the meters to be read; treat the office separately as the starting depot.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the depot node corresponding to the utility office where the crew begins the walk. This node is the fixed start of the tour used to compute arrival times.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a specific water meter location. Used to reference that meter when specifying the visit order and computing arrival times.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: The x coordinate of the meter's position in the shared coordinate system (e.g., easting). Combined with y to compute walking distances and hence arrival times.

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: The y coordinate of the meter's position in the shared coordinate system (e.g., northing). Combined with x to compute walking distances and hence arrival times.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of locations in this instance, including the regional office (the depot) and all retail outlets the sales rep must visit. Use this to know how many nodes the tour must cover.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the depot node corresponding to the regional office where the sales representative starts the tour (and may return at the end). This ID matches one of the node_id entries for the locations list.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a location entry; represents either a retail outlet or the regional office. Matches the depot field when this entry is the starting office.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: The x coordinate of the location on the map (planar coordinate system). Used together with the y coordinate to compute travel distances and thereby arrival times between stops.

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: The y coordinate of the location on the map (planar coordinate system). Together with the x coordinate, it defines the location of an outlet or the office for distance/time calculations.
